title: Sports Day
strapline: On your marks — running, jumping, balancing and cheering each other on.
intent: A sports day gives children a joyful reason to run, jump, throw, balance and move their whole bodies with purpose.
Taking part, having a go and finishing the race build determination, confidence and physical control.
Cheering friends on and taking turns grows cooperation, good sportsmanship and warmth towards others.
Simple races and challenges weave in counting, ordering, measuring and comparing.
The day celebrates effort and joining in over winning — everyone's a champion for trying.
implementation: Set out a range of physical challenges — running, jumping, beanbag throw, egg-and-spoon, balance beam, obstacle course.
Keep the spirit on effort and fun: 'You did it — you ran all the way! Well done for having a go!'
Invite children to cheer each other on and take turns, celebrating everyone's tries.
Weave in maths lightly — count the jumps, measure the throw, who finished first, second, third.
Offer challenges at every level so every child can take part and feel successful.
Follow the children — some will race everything twice, others will practise the balance beam all morning.
key_questions: Which challenge would you like to try first?
How far can you throw the beanbag — shall we measure?
How did your body feel after running so fast?
How can we cheer on our friends?
What was tricky — how did you keep going?

impact.text: Children run, jump, throw and balance with growing control and confidence.
Children keep trying at challenges and take pride in having a go.
Children cheer others on, take turns and show good sportsmanship.
Children count, measure and order in the challenges.
Children notice what their bodies need after exercise.

enhancements: A circuit of physical challenges — running, jumping, throwing, balancing.
An egg-and-spoon and beanbag-throw with measuring tapes and markers.
An obstacle course to negotiate and time.
Medals or ribbons for effort and taking part, made by the children.
A cheering and water-station role so everyone has a part to play.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into running, jumping and every physical challenge.
They test what their bodies can do with joy.
active_learning: Children keep trying, finishing races and mastering the balance beam.
They persist at a challenge until they can do it.
creating_thinking: Children work out how to jump further or balance longer.
They think about how to cheer on and include their friends.
